docs.title: Verification
docs.text: Static checks and the isolated native asset validator for Hytale 0.7.7 passed. Native asset warnings remain. The custom portal's obsolete Flags.IsUsable field was removed. Check rendering, hand positioning, and transitions in-game.

docs.title: Resource structure
docs.text:
Hytale stores inventory icons separately from model textures. The native Icons/ItemsGenerated folder is flat. Custom icons are organized under Common/Icons/Items/.

  • Tools/Hatchet/, Tools/Hoe/, and Tools/Pickaxe/ for tool icons.
  • Weapons/Wand/ for wand icons.
  • Resources/Ores/ for ore icons.

Models and texture atlases remain in Common/Items/Tools/<Typ>/, Common/Items/Weapons/Wand/HytaleCity/, and the custom Common/Items/Resources/ categories. Use the same capitalization for Pickaxe everywhere. Item definitions under Server/Item/Items use paths relative to Common. The generator writes wand icons to the new locations. Validation checks exact path spelling even on Windows and checks the ZIP for obsolete resources.

All HC_ item IDs remain valid with the directory change, so no additional database migration is needed. Replace the old pack during installation. Static reference and ZIP checks passed after the restructure. A new native server and client test is pending.

docs.title: Hotbar icon and shaft connection
docs.text: Wands use dedicated _Icon64.png files without an IconProperties transform. Internal connector pieces close the gap at the end and connect the shaft to the head. Existing shapes and item IDs are preserved. Static checks confirm continuous shaft geometry and valid icon paths. Rendering still needs client verification.

docs.title: Native icon format and resources
docs.text: Custom item icons are 64 × 64 RGBA PNGs, matching the 4,537 native generated item icons in the tested assets. Older wand icons were 128 × 128. The generator and validator enforce the native size and new _Icon64.png paths avoid reusing older files. Custom material and ore textures live under Common/Items/Resources/Materials/Ingot_Textures and Common/Items/Resources/Ores/Ores_Texture. References to native models under Resources/... remain valid. Verify rendering after replacing the pack and restarting.

docs.title: Model atlases at 128 × 128
docs.text: All 19 custom model textures use 128 × 128 RGBA. The 19 item icons remain 64 × 64. Atlas expansion preserves previous pixels at their UV positions and extends edge pixels to fill the new area. It adds no texture detail and leaves model scale unchanged. The pack build runs prepare_textures.py and the validator enforces both formats. Live testing of the atlas expansion is pending.

docs.title: Commands and permissions
docs.text:
Replace required placeholders such as <player> with actual values. See the current server help for optional arguments and their allowed positions.

Area Entry / Subcommands plots /plots, /plot buy, /plot info, /plot list, /plot rename <old> <new>, /plot selltocity <plot> Plot cooperation /plot invite, /plot invites, /plot offer, and /plot offers with the matching accept and decline subcommands Plot limits /plot limit get, set, increase, and reset with a target player and a limit where applicable Homes /homes, /sethome, /home <name>, /home remove <name> Money /money, /money send <player> <amount>; Admin: add, remove, set Jobs /job <jobKey>, /job enter <jobKey>, /job info, /job sell <amount|all> Jobs-Admin /job admin item, milestones, shop, upgrades, npcset <jobKey> NPCs /hcnpc, set [identifier] <job> <type> [name], reset [identifier], reload Enchanting /enchant item [enchantment] [value] HUD /hud Inbox /inbox Teleport request /tpa <player>, /tpaccept, /tpdeny World Warps /warp city, /warp farmworld, /warp spawn Protection /protection register <areaName> <actionType>, /protection remove <areaName>, /protection list Help /rules, /tutorial

For AFK, PlayerStats and the general level system, no registered player command is documented in the current sources.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
HcNpcs administration and Jobs NPC selection require hcnpcs.admin. The enchantment test command belongs to hytale:WorldEditor. Check other administrative permissions against the registered Hytale commands.

requireNoPermission() removes the additional command permission requirement. Ownership, balance, limit, and service checks still apply. Apply them to both commands and UI actions.

See the HcNpcs command guide for complete NPC syntax and the inventory for command classes.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• A Hytale server build compatible with API 0.7.7 and Java 25.
  • MariaDB for Core and the plugins based on it.
  • Matching Hytale assets for the referenced roles, models, and item IDs.
  • Backups of the existing database, worlds, and plugin data before updates.

docs.title: Installation order
docs.text:
1. Prepare core configuration files in the core data directory used by the server.
  2. Install the Core JAR and verify that the plugin and database initialize successfully.
  3. Install the required gameplay JARs. Use compatible versions of Jobs, HcNpcs, Economy, Inbox, PlayerHud, and Core. Install the custom asset pack.
  4. Prepare spawn, city and, if required, farmworld to match the commands used.
  5. Check profiles, money, teleports, plots, jobs and UIs with a test player.

Hytale determines load order from manifest dependencies. Deploy the built plugin JARs only. The original-*.jar files and build dependencies are not separate plugins.

docs.title: Plugin data directories
docs.text:
Plugins with active file configuration use CorePlugin, AfkPlugin, JobsPlugin, and LevelPlugin within the server's existing plugin data directory. The file paths drop the HytaleCity_ prefix. Plugin IDs such as HytaleCity:CorePlugin stay the same.

Update Core, AFK, Jobs, and Level together. The next startup automatically migrates existing HytaleCity_* directories to the short names.

Level also checks com.hytalecity_LevelPlugin. It imports missing player files and gives the current config precedence over the older one. Merges archive old directories under .config-backups. Conflicting files are preserved and normally stop startup before migration. Older secondary Level data is the exception and its original is archived.

Hytale modules keep their own directories, such as Hytale_Shop and Hytale_HytaleGenerator. Some gameplay plugins do not need a data directory.

docs.title: Core files
docs.text:
File YAML root Purpose database.yml database JDBC driver, URL, credentials, and pool coreConfig.yml coreConfig Height, plot size, prices, name length, limits, and starting balance jobConfig.yml jobConfig Shared profession XP curve and legacy balance values. Quests and milestones are stored in MariaDB.

Example using placeholders:

database:
  driver: org.mariadb.jdbc.Driver
  url: jdbc:mariadb://DB_HOST:3306/DB_NAME
  username: DB_USER
  password: REPLACE_LOCALLY
  pool:
    maximumPoolSize: 10
    minimumIdle: 2
    idleTimeout: 30000
    maxLifetime: 1800000

This example covers the database. Provide the other two files as well and use values accepted by their configuration validators. Enter production credentials locally and keep logs and configuration copies private.

docs.title: Plugin-specific settings
docs.text:
• AFK: afk.json, validated live reload.
  • Level: config.json accepts maxLevel, startLevel, and scalingExponent. Core provides the fixed curve coefficients and overflow settings.
  • Jobs: Shop offers and upgrade recipes live in the database. Keep any existing job-shop-offers.json and job-upgrades.json for the one-time import on first startup.
  • FarmWorld: embedded worldConfig.json; the reset time is currently set in the code.
  • HcNpcs: NPC assignments live in the database. HcNpcs/config.json sets interactionDistanceMeters, which defaults to 3.0. Apply edits with /hcnpc reload.

Check each plugin page to see which files the plugin actually reads. A bundled config.json alone does not indicate active configuration.

docs.title: Database migrations
docs.text: Core owns all database access. MariaDB is the supported database. Spring starts Liquibase (db/changelog/db.changelog-master.xml) before the EntityManagerFactory, then Hibernate runs validate. Never enable update as a workaround for a failed migration.

docs.title: First deployment
docs.text:
1. Stop the Hytale server and back up MariaDB, plugin configuration and worlds.
  2. Deploy the matching CorePlugin, JobsPlugin and HC asset pack together.
  3. Keep existing JobsPlugin/job-shop-offers.json and job-upgrades.json in the server plugin data directory for this first start.
  4. Start the server. Liquibase adopts existing tables using guarded baseline changesets, creates absent tables/indexes/constraints, applies one-time seeds and renames exact custom item IDs to HC_. Existing incompatible column layouts or unique-key collisions fail startup; inspect the error rather than dropping data or clearing DATABASECHANGELOG.
  5. Jobs imports each legacy JSON file transactionally through Core, recording a data_import_markers entry. Only after commit does it move the source to .imported-catalog/. Invalid data leaves the file and transaction unchanged. Archive failure does not repeat a committed import.
  6. Check startup, shop/upgrade admin saves, NPC UI and actual inventory operations in the Hytale client.

Shop offers and upgrade recipes now live in job_catalog_entries and job_catalog_requirements. Core returns immutable snapshots; Jobs refreshes a read cache every five seconds and performs admin writes on its catalog IO worker. The legacy job page retains its enabled-items fallback for Tools. NPC purchases use job_merchant_stock. No shop JSON is written or regenerated.

A missing legacy file keeps bundled defaults. An explicit legacy file, even an empty list, replaces unmodified DEFAULT entries of that kind. Existing ADMIN/IMPORT entries win on matching keys. Four Farmer upgrade defaults are seeded once from the supplied config, with HC_ identifiers. Shop offers have no invented defaults. Import markers prevent reimport; deleting an entry is permanent across restarts. Editing or copying an already-imported JSON is not a supported update path; use the admin UI or Core API.

docs.title: Professions and merchants
docs.text: Core migrations V4–V8 create profession tracking, daily offers, inventory receipts, merchant stock, level rewards and collection rules. V6 preserves prior award records. V7 reuses item totals for valid collection actions. V8 adds Cook, Fisher, and the Farmer wheat and rice content. See quest and reward maintenance.

docs.title: Core API
docs.text:
JobCatalogService.listAll(), save(JobCatalogRecord), delete(kind, job, category, item) and importOnce(source, kind, rows) own persistence. Kind is SHOP or UPGRADE. Imports use a stable source key and commit all rows with their marker. Costs are nonnegative, amounts positive, requirements merged by item (at most eight). Physical legacy asset IDs are canonicalized on writes; logical enchantment family keys such as vibranium_hoe stay unchanged.

V9 adds player_inbox_messages for notifications, read status, and archive status. Include the table in regular MariaDB backups. Inbox

docs.title: Asset migration
docs.text:
The versioned HC migration updates items, upgrade/enchantment references, catalog entries/requirements, sold-item totals, unlocks, milestone definitions/rewards and claim item references. IDs of definitions/players and balances are retained. JSON rewards replace complete quoted identifiers, not arbitrary substrings. Unique-key collisions abort the DML changeset and require reconciliation. Historical serialized inventory evidence and physical world/inventory data are not rewritten; pending sales must be reviewed before changing physical inventory asset IDs.

This code prepares the production migration; local tests do not imply the live server database has already been updated.

docs.title: Future changes
docs.text: Add a new numbered changelog include for every schema/data change, update matching JPA mappings, and test fresh and existing MariaDB plus a second startup. Never edit an already deployed changeset or old seed file: Liquibase verifies checksums. Use one-time seeds for fixed initial values, not recurring overwrites of operator-managed data. Keep DATABASECHANGELOG and DATABASECHANGELOGLOCK in backups. MariaDB DDL is not globally transactional; recovery from an interrupted schema change uses guarded steps and a backup, not a promise of full DDL rollback.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: Normal mvnw test runs the Core suite. JobCatalogMigrationTest requires an explicitly supplied -Dhc.testDbPort=<port> on a dedicated disposable localhost MariaDB instance (root password hytale-local-test). It creates uniquely named test databases, tests new schema, adoption, HC renames, import rollback, admin precedence and restart idempotence. Never point it at production. SchemaExportTest is an opt-in developer aid (-Dhc.exportSchema=true); exported SQL does not change the frozen migrations automatically.

docs.title: Creating profession quests and rewards
docs.text: These examples use the MariaDB Core database with migrations V4 through V8 applied. Try the steps on a test server first. For rollout to multiple servers, put the SQL in a new Core Liquibase migration so the existing checksums stay intact.

docs.title: Add a quest
docs.text:
1. Choose a profession and a unique quest ID. The profession keys are Farmer, Holzfäller, Miner, Jäger, Koch, and Fischer.
  2. Set the title, minimum level, money, and positive profession XP in job_quest_templates.
  3. Add at least one goal in job_quest_goals. The example counts six gold ore blocks in basalt mined by the player and also requires delivery of four pieces of gold ore.
  4. Open the merchant with an active Miner profession at level 10 or above. For a quick test, use a fresh test profile or wait for the next daily rotation. Whether the new template appears depends on that day's selection.
START TRANSACTION;

INSERT INTO job_quest_templates
    (quest_key, job_key, title, min_level, reward_money, reward_xp, enabled)
VALUES
    ('mine_basalt_gold', 'Miner', 'Gold aus dem Basalt', 10, 160, 40, TRUE);

INSERT INTO job_quest_goals (quest_key, goal_type, target_key, goal_amount)
VALUES
    ('mine_basalt_gold', 'BREAK', 'Ore_Gold_Basalt', 6),
    ('mine_basalt_gold', 'DELIVER', 'Ore_Gold', 4);

COMMIT;
Goal type target_key When it counts DELIVER Inventory item ID such as Ore_Gold or a custom item The quantity is taken from the player's inventory on delivery. BREAK Block ID such as Ore_Gold_Basalt The matching natural block is successfully mined after accepting the quest. HARVEST Base plant ID such as Plant_Crop_Carrot_Block A mature plant is harvested after accepting the quest. HUNT NPC role such as Boar An eligible wild animal is killed after accepting the quest. CRAFT Primary recipe output item ID Counts a successful crafting event.

For action goals, an asterisk matches all eligible activities of the profession. Progress requires a matching rule in job_activity_rules. A collection rule in job_collection_rules alone is insufficient. Every goal must be met in full. Deliveries can also come from stored goods or player trades.

The merchant stores up to three offers per player and profession per calendar day in Europe/Berlin. Two quests can be open at once. The active profession determines eligibility for acceptance, action progress, and delivery. Open quests survive both profession changes and daily rotations. Titles, goals, and rewards are copied at acceptance, so changes to a template affect future acceptances. Set enabled to FALSE to remove a template from rotation while keeping existing quests playable.

docs.title: Update a quest
docs.text:
Update the template and its goals in one transaction. Accepted quests retain their stored copy.

START TRANSACTION;
UPDATE job_quest_templates
SET reward_money=190, reward_xp=50
WHERE quest_key='mine_basalt_gold' AND job_key='Miner';
UPDATE job_quest_goals SET goal_amount=8
WHERE quest_key='mine_basalt_gold' AND goal_type='BREAK' AND target_key='Ore_Gold_Basalt';
COMMIT;

docs.title: Change a level milestone reward
docs.text:
The merchant's level milestones screen lets players claim each reached milestone once. job_level_milestones sets the money amount. job_level_milestone_items adds item IDs and quantities. The example sets a cash reward and two Vibranium bars for Miner level 25.

START TRANSACTION;

INSERT INTO job_level_milestones (job_key, required_level, reward_money)
VALUES ('Miner', 25, 1500)
ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE reward_money=VALUES(reward_money);

INSERT INTO job_level_milestone_items (job_key, required_level, item_key, quantity)
VALUES ('Miner', 25, 'HC_Ingredient_Bar_Vibranium', 2)
ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE quantity=VALUES(quantity);

COMMIT;

If needed, delete the old item row for the same profession and level using its old item ID. Set the money amount to zero for an item-only reward. Check the ID against the installed pack and test claiming with a full inventory, then with free space. Previously claimed milestones stay claimed when you edit rewards. Claims are recorded in job_level_milestone_awards.

docs.title: Change a collection milestone reward
docs.text:
1. Run /job admin milestones with an admin account.
  2. Select a profession and item. Enter the required collection quantity, money, profession XP, and any item rewards.
  3. Separate multiple item rewards with commas. HC_Ingredient_Bar_Vibranium:2 grants two bars. Omitting the quantity grants one.
  4. Save and verify the row on the merchant's collection milestones screen or with /job info. Test the claim with a separate test profile.

Collection definitions live in job_milestone_definitions, progress in player_job_item_totals, and claims in player_job_milestone_claims. To add a collection item, map the server-side action to its item ID through job_collection_rules and enable the item for that profession in items. Edit live milestones with care because changes to quantities, order, or selection can affect the claim key.

docs.title: Database startup
docs.text:
Hytale can wrap Spring or Hikari INFO and WARN lines from stderr in SEVERE [SERR]. Check the underlying level and exception. HikariPool ... Start completed indicates successful pool initialization.

For Connection refused, check reachability, listener, container port, and JDBC address. Check the user and permissions for authentication failures. Redact credentials when sharing logs.

docs.title: Custom UI connection failure
docs.text:
Failed to load Custom UI documents indicates a client load error. Check recently changed .ui files, resource paths, and Hytale's template structure. Java compilation does not validate this syntax.

If the crash only occurs on a button action, check event payloads and attempts to read unsupported UI properties. See the UI guide.

docs.title: Store processing and slow world tasks
docs.text:
Store is currently processing means a mutation ran in an unsuitable ECS processing phase. Move it to the correct CommandBuffer or a later task on the world executor and handle the underlying error.

Task took ... ms identifies a slow task. Distinguish database IO, blocking waits, chunk loading, and garbage collection. Ensure that join tracking and profile creation do not count the same join twice.

docs.title: Network and authentication
docs.text:
The Linux host sets the UDP receive buffer limit separately from the Java heap. Check net.core.rmem_max and, if needed, set it in a file under /etc/sysctl.d/. Use the value required by the server warning and verify its effect on the host and container.

invalid_grant with an expired Hytale downloader refresh token relates to downloader authentication. The server may exit before loading plugins. Resolve the downloader's sign-in state.

docs.title: Assets and third-party plugins
docs.text:
Investigate duplicate asset ID warnings using the paths in the log. Even packs containing custom content can include copied or conflicting IDs. Plugin configuration folders are separate from asset packs and may have no asset manifest.

External plugins can generate version warnings. Check the plugin and filename in the log before assigning the issue to Core.

docs.title: Legacy HcNpcs spawn attempts
docs.text: Could not spawn NPC city.lumberjack paired with Unknown or invalid NPC role: holzfaeller comes from a legacy database spawn definition. Current HcNpcs ignores role-based definitions at load and has removed spawn and despawn logic. Stop the server, replace the HcNpcs JAR, and restart. Existing native bindings and display names are retained without manually deleting data.

docs.title: HcNpcs shutdown after world shutdown
docs.text: World thread is not accepting tasks occurred when a world had already stopped before HcNpcs could remove its interaction hints. HcNpcs now skips these rejected tasks, including when Hytale wraps the exception. Active worlds still clean up through their own queues. Shutdown clears local caches and closing again has no effect. ECS work never falls back to the shutdown thread.

docs.title: Before replacing plugins
docs.text:
Check versions and manifest dependencies. Keep Core, HcNpcs, and Jobs on compatible versions. Back up the database and affected world and configuration files, then verify that the backups can be restored.

On a test server, check startup, schema changes, migration, NPCs, sales, and UIs. Deploy the same built JARs after validation. Compare checksums to confirm that the copied JARs match.

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text:
• General player levels are imported from legacy JSON through Core. The database then becomes the source of truth.
  • Job NPCs are imported from jobs_npc_job_keys into Core definitions and actions. Existing definitions take precedence, including deliberately reset mappings.
  • The schema adds player_jobs.version with a default of 0 for existing data.

Disable the NPC definition or remove the specific action to turn it off. Deleting the definition can allow a legacy assignment to reappear on import.

docs.title: Open sales
docs.text:
State Meaning and action PREPARED Removal may have occurred. Check the inventory plan and actual stacks. COMMITTED The database has applied the rewards. Do not refund automatically. REFUND_DUE Refund is pending or may be partial. Reconcile what was actually returned. ABORTED No payout is outstanding and the refund or absence of removal is confirmed.

Use JobSaleService.pending, diagnostic, commit, abort, and confirmRefund for reconciliation. Confirm a refund after returning the items or verifying that no removal took place. A repeated abort does not authorize a second physical refund.

Inventory and world files cannot commit atomically with MariaDB. After an ambiguous interruption, check the operation ID before returning any items. See the full contract.

docs.title: Plugin overview
docs.text:
Plugin Responsibility CorePlugin Provides the Spring context, database access, and shared services through MainCore.getBean(...). CityBuildPlugin Provides plot commands and menus. Core plot services enforce rules and persist data. HomePlugin Manages personal teleport destinations through Core and provides the homes page. EconomyPlugin Provides commands for the shared Core balance used by professions, plots, and rewards. InboxPlugin Personal inbox for server notifications. JobsPlugin Provides professions, XP, sales, merchant pages, shops, upgrades, and milestones. Requires CorePlugin and HcNpcs. Enchantments is optional. LevelPlugin Adapts general progression to Hytale. Core stores progress and rewards. HcNpcs Connects existing native NPCs to plugin actions and custom UIs. Core stores bindings and Hytale owns the NPC lifecycle. EnchantmentsPlugin Manages enchantment rolls, upgrade rolls, conflicts, and item effects. Core provides shared definitions and item data. PlayerStatsPlugin Collects player events and persists batches through Core. PlayerStats counts joins and leaves, while Core creates profiles. PlayerHudPlugin Shows shared player data in a Hytale HUD. /hud toggles it. The UI is in Hud/PlayerHud.ui. AfkPlugin Disconnects inactive players after a warning and grace period. The timer starts after PlayerReady and resets on activity. TeleportPlugin Manages teleport requests between players. WarpPlugin Provides fixed destinations via /warp city, /warp farmworld, and /warp spawn. FarmWorldPlugin Runs the renewable resource world farmworld and its reset scheduler. It currently declares no Core dependency. ProtectionPlugin Associates protected areas with allowed and blocked actions. Core owns the shared data and decisions. DocumentationPlugin Displays help in the Hytale client. MkDocs builds this website separately.

See the inventory for manifest dependencies, artifacts, and source revisions. Check each plugin's documentation to see whether it reads or reloads a bundled config.json.

docs.title: AfkPlugin
docs.text: AFK detects inactivity and disconnects players after a warning and a full grace period. The timer starts after PlayerReady and resets when activity is detected.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The active configuration is afk.json in the plugin data directory. Relevant fields include idleSeconds, warnSeconds, checkIntervalMillis, movementThreshold, kickMessage, and warnMessage. The code defaults to short test values of ten seconds each for inactivity and the warning grace period. Set appropriate values for regular operation.

The plugin watches for changes and applies them after validation. Invalid edits leave the last valid configuration active. The old afk_backup.json is an inactive backup.

docs.title: Timing and display
docs.text:
With ten seconds of inactivity and a ten-second grace period, the player is kicked approximately 20 seconds after the last activity, plus polling and tick delays. The full grace period starts when the warning is actually shown. Movement, changes in view direction, and registered interactions count as activity.

The warning is a notification. The plugin queues the disconnect on the world executor outside current Store processing. Whether Hytale displays the reason on the Connection Closed screen depends on the client and transport. In the tested version, the native kick also showed only the lost connection.

The plugin logs errors and invalid configurations. Routine startup, timer, warning, and successful reload messages are omitted from logs. Player warnings and timers continue to work.

docs.title: CityBuildPlugin
docs.text: CityBuild provides plot commands and the plot menu. Core plot services handle persistence and enforce the rules.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: /plots opens the menu. The /plot subcommands cover purchasing, details, listings, renaming, selling to the city, and inviting or making offers to other players. See commands.

docs.title: Integration
docs.text:
Purchasing and selling affect the shared balance. Core defines limits and prices. Co-ownership, invitations, and offers are persisted in Core and follow the same rules from every interface.

Renaming rejects duplicate names among the player's plots. The interface reports the conflict without sending an invalid state to the client or applying a conflicting database update.

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
Common/UI/Custom/Plots/Plots.ui is a Hytale UI document. Dynamic data and event values follow the UI contracts. Test the list, forms, and rapid clicks in the actual client after building.

Plot boundaries use the custom asset HC_Plot_Border_Particle. Update CityBuild when switching to the pack version with HC_ identifiers.

docs.title: CorePlugin
docs.text: Core provides the shared Spring context, database access, and domain services. Other plugins access these services through MainCore.getBean(...).

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Create player records on first contact and provide profiles and ranks.
  • Manage money, plot and home limits, plots, offers, invitations, and protected areas.
  • Store professions, profession XP, item totals, milestone definitions and claims, shop offers, upgrade recipes, and enchantment definitions. The database is the sole source for milestone definitions.
  • Manage general player levels, XP operations, and persistent level rewards.
  • Store NPC definitions, actions, and prepared or committed sales.
  • Apply statistics batches atomically with stable operation identifiers for retries.

docs.title: Configuration and boundaries
docs.text:
Core reads database.yml, coreConfig.yml, and jobConfig.yml from its data directory. Their YAML roots are database, coreConfig, and jobConfig, respectively. These files do not have full live reload support.

Core uses versioned Liquibase migrations and one-time seeds. Hibernate checks the schema with validate. Back up existing databases and test recovery before changing them. General player levels and profession levels use separate systems. See migrating existing databases and configuration.

See also Core APIs and data storage.

docs.title: DocumentationPlugin
docs.text: This gameplay plugin displays help in the Hytale client. MkDocs builds this website separately.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
/rules opens the rules and /tutorial opens the introduction. The interfaces are in Rules/Rules.ui and Tutorial/Tutorial.ui.

The manifest currently declares no Core dependency. Help pages are UI and content assets served by the plugin.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:
When adding a player-facing feature, review both the in-game help and the public technical documentation. Keep rules, documented commands, and actual permissions aligned.

Hytale parses the .ui files with its own parser. Test changes to layout, line breaks, or components in the client. See the UI guide.

docs.title: EconomyPlugin
docs.text: Economy provides the command layer for the shared Core account. Jobs, plot purchases, level rewards, and other systems use that same balance.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
/money shows the money section. /money send <player> <amount> transfers funds. The administrative subcommands are add, remove, and set, each taking a player and amount. Check the permissions registered in Hytale before granting access.

Players receive balance, transfer, and administrative booking feedback as notifications. A successful transfer creates an inbox entry for both parties. The admin console still receives text feedback.

docs.title: Core contract
docs.text:
getBalance, deposit, withdraw, setBalance, and transferMoney return BalanceResult. Always check isSuccess(). Invalid amounts, missing players, insufficient funds, and overflow are errors.

Balance writes lock the player's row. Transfers lock both players in a stable order. Transferring money to yourself cannot increase the balance.

A database transfer alone cannot guarantee atomic item delivery. Callers that also deliver items need their own inventory and recovery contract.

docs.title: EnchantmentsPlugin
docs.text: Enchantments manages random enchantments, upgrade rolls, conflicts, and behavior-driven item effects. Core provides definitions and shared item and upgrade data.

docs.title: Public interface
docs.text:
EnchantmentsApi.service() returns the service. Use serviceOrEmpty() for an optional integration. EnchantmentsService includes upgradeAndRoll, rollSingleEnchantment, applyRollResultToItem, setEnchantments, getEnchantments, getEnchantmentKeys, getUpgradeLevel, and applyBehaviors.

Rolls consider the item type, existing enchantments, and upgrade level. The resulting item state is stored under the metadata namespace hytale_city_enchantments. Preserve this metadata when copying, reserving, or refunding items.

docs.title: Usage and limitations
docs.text:
Jobs can integrate the plugin for upgrades. Effects run through the trigger and rule implementation and enchantment-behaviors.json. Check the behavior implementation for each effect you intend to use.

/enchant item [enchantment] [value] is an administrative or test command assigned to the hytale:WorldEditor group.

docs.title: FarmWorldPlugin
docs.text: FarmWorldPlugin runs the renewable resource world farmworld and schedules its resets. It currently declares no Core dependency.

docs.title: Current reset flow
docs.text:
The code schedules a reset every day at 05:00 in the server's time zone. A warning is sent five minutes beforehand. The plugin reads world settings from the bundled worldConfig.json and assigns a new seed when it creates the replacement world.

The current code schedules returning players to spawn, removes the old world, deletes its storage path, and creates it again. Verify that players actually reach spawn before deletion.

docs.title: Operations and limitations
docs.text:
farmworld is renewable. Keep permanent player buildings in designated worlds or plots. Before enabling resets, verify the destination world, spawn, and backups.

There is no general transactional minigame instance manager yet. Round-based arenas need their own lifecycle. See minigames.

docs.title: HomePlugin
docs.text: HomePlugin manages personal teleport destinations through Core and provides a dedicated homes page.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
• /sethome creates a home at the current position. See Hytale command help for the optional name.
  • /home <name> teleports to a named home.
  • /home remove <name> removes a home.
  • /homes opens the interface.

docs.title: Data and integration
docs.text:
HomeService manages saved homes. The shared Core player profile determines limits. Destination world, position, and owner are persisted domain data.

The UI is in Homes/Homes.ui. After database work, the teleport still requires a valid destination world and player session. Future minigames will also need a session check. There is no shared lock for active rounds yet.

docs.title: InboxPlugin
docs.text:
Open your personal inbox with /inbox. The tabs are Ungelesen (Unread), Alle (All), and Archiv (Archive). The inbox opens on Alle, with newest messages first. Money messages appear in the same views as other notifications.

Opening a message marks it as read. You can mark all messages as read, archive individual messages, restore them from the archive, and sort by newest, oldest, or unread first. Messages and their read and archive status survive reconnects. The HUD shows the command and the unread count.

docs.title: Installation and storage
docs.text:
Install InboxPlugin with a compatible CorePlugin. Migration V9 creates player_inbox_messages in MariaDB. Install compatible Economy and HUD versions for their inbox integration.

Core records outbound server notification packets for the recipient, including notifications sent directly by plugins. Chat messages and other UI event types are outside this capture path. Capture starts with the updated Core. Economy records successful transfers and administrative balance changes in the same transaction as the balance update. Core skips the corresponding tagged toasts when recording outgoing packets, so the booking is shown once.

docs.title: JobsPlugin
docs.text:
Jobs requires Core and HcNpcs. A merchant NPC's profession menu offers selling, buying, quests, profession selection, and milestones.

Profession NPC type Activity that grants profession XP Farmer farmer Harvest mature crops Lumberjack lumberjack Break naturally generated logs in the farm world Hunter hunter Kill eligible wild animals in the farm world Miner miner Mine naturally generated ore blocks in the farm world Cook cook Make bread, vegetable skewers, meat skewers, or pumpkin pie at a cooking bench Fisher fisher Catch salmon, rainbow trout, pike, or catfish in the farm world

docs.title: Activating and switching professions
docs.text:
Activate a profession in the profession menu or with /job enter <jobKey>. Only one profession is active at a time. Unlocked professions, XP, and open quests are retained when switching. The XP curve rises exponentially through level 25 and linearly afterward. The system supports at least level 1000. Overall player progression has its own curve.

Use /hcnpc set [identifier] merchant <type> [name] to make an NPC a merchant. /job admin npcset <jobKey> binds the next targeted NPC within 60 seconds and requires hcnpcs.admin. The NPC keeps its native role. See HcNpcs setup.

docs.title: Progress and rewards
docs.text:
• Quests offer up to three daily choices per player and profession. Offers change at midnight in Europe/Berlin. Two quests per profession can be open at the same time. Cook and Fisher each start with eight templates. Farmer has eleven templates, including new wheat and rice quests. The other professions each start with eight templates. Open quests carry over to the next day.
  • Level milestones offer claimable rewards at levels 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 150, 200, 500, and 1000. Money and items are configured in MariaDB. Previously paid rewards remain recorded as claimed.
  • Collection milestones count eligible actions. For example, mining natural gold ore in basalt increases the gold count. Hunters also get credit for producing light leather and killing eligible wild animals for fur. Picking up, dropping, and selling items do not increase these counts. Player-placed logs and ore blocks are excluded. Mining works both in the fixed farm world and in playable instances of its template. /job info opens the separate collection overview.

Create quests and rewards · Add a profession

Farmer retains existing progress and gains wheat and rice as collection targets and merchant goods. Fisher earns XP and collection credit by killing configured wild fish. Fish traps supply goods for some delivery quests and sales. Emptying a trap does not currently award profession progress.

Item catalog

docs.title: Trade
docs.text:
Merchants buy enabled goods for their profession at the base price. The confirmation shows the quantity and total proceeds. Players can trade without activating the profession. The buy menu shows stock shared by profession and item. It refills daily up to its configured limit. Selling earns money. Profession activities and quests award XP.

/job sell <amount|all> sells the held item type after a second confirmation within 30 seconds. The merchant menu uses the same sale flow for items selected from the inventory.

In the Beruf tab, the button for inactive professions is labeled Job annehmen. The English job types in the table also work with /job enter <jobKey> and /job admin npcset <jobKey>. Trade confirmations appear as notifications and are recorded in the inbox.

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
Table Contents items Trade goods and base prices job_merchant_stock Purchase prices, stock, capacity, and daily refill job_activity_rules Profession XP and eligible quest actions job_collection_rules Mapping from actions to collection items job_quest_templates, job_quest_goals Quest templates and goals job_level_milestones, job_level_milestone_items Level thresholds and rewards job_milestone_definitions Collection thresholds and rewards

The previous shop and upgrade view is available via /job <jobKey> for unlocked professions. Its offers and recipes live in job_catalog_entries and job_catalog_requirements. After the one-time JSON import, maintain these through the admin UIs or the Core API. See migration and import.

docs.title: LevelPlugin
docs.text: LevelPlugin adapts general player progression to Hytale. Core now stores progression and rewards in place of periodically saved player JSON.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
XP requirements follow connected quadratic curve segments. Players level up as soon as they reach the threshold. One grant can advance several levels and records rewards for intermediate levels.

The default range is level 1 to 50. config.json in the Level data directory contains only maxLevel, startLevel, and scalingExponent. Core fixes the curve coefficients and overflow cap. A curve change must preserve existing progression.

docs.title: Integration
docs.text:
New plugins should use Core's AsyncLevelService. Changes report success after database commit. Reuse the operation UUID when retrying grants. The Level adapter also provides futures and local LevelUp and LevelDown callbacks.

Old player files are imported idempotently and retained as backups. The HUD displays the overall player level and the active profession separately.

See the level API reference for methods, curves, imports, and rewards.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
{
  "maxLevel": 50,
  "startLevel": 1,
  "scalingExponent": 0.35
}

At startup the plugin rewrites valid legacy files to the three supported fields, preserving their values and the default curve. autosaveIntervalSeconds and logging.debug already had no effect. Curve and overflow settings are also ignored now. Invalid and malformed files are preserved.

docs.title: What does scalingExponent do?
docs.text:
scalingExponent affects the XP awarded by scaled grants. The XP needed to level up is independent, and 0.35 does not mean a fixed 35 percent increase per level.

Awarded XP = base XP × (current level XP threshold / level 1 XP threshold)^scalingExponent
  • 0 disables level-dependent scaling.
  • 0.35 applies moderate scaling. At level 10, 100 base XP becomes approximately 191 XP.
  • 1 scales awards proportionally to the XP threshold.

Direct grants via grantRawExp stay unscaled. The fixed curve requires 150 XP from level 1 to 2, 191 from level 2 to 3, and 244 from level 3 to 4. General player levels and profession levels remain independent.

docs.title: Assigning jobs to custom NPCs
docs.text:
Create the NPC with Hytale's native tools. HcNpcs binds a function and profession type to that NPC and opens the appropriate custom UI on interaction.

Required permission: hcnpcs.admin.

docs.title: Assign an NPC
docs.text:
Aim at the NPC and enter:

/hcnpc set merchant lumberjack
/hcnpc set merchant miner "Peter"

The NPC under the crosshair must be within the configured interaction distance, three meters by default. Alternatively, pass its entity UUID or an existing HcNpcs key:

/hcnpc set <identifier> merchant lumberjack
/hcnpc set <identifier> merchant miner "Peter"

Full syntax:

/hcnpc set [identifier] <job> <type> [name]

An explicit identifier takes precedence over the NPC under the crosshair. Display names are not identifiers. /hcnpc lists saved keys, UUIDs, and assignments. New assignments currently use keys such as legacy.<UUID>.

A new UUID binding requires a loaded NPC in your world. An existing key can be reassigned without changing the name even if the NPC is unloaded. The NPC must be loaded for a name change so the original name can be captured.

docs.title: Available jobs
docs.text:
Job Function merchant Opens the chosen profession's merchant UI, including selling its goods.

Only merchant is currently implemented. Additional functions need a registered provider.

docs.title: Available profession types
docs.text:
Type in command Profession farmer Farmer lumberjack Lumberjack hunter Hunter miner Miner cook Cook fisher Fisher

Examples:

/hcnpc set merchant farmer "Farmer"
/hcnpc set merchant lumberjack "Holzhändler"
/hcnpc set merchant hunter "Jagdhändler"
/hcnpc set merchant miner "Erzhändler"

The type selects the profession and its UI content. The NPC retains its model and native role.

docs.title: Optional display name
docs.text:
The final argument sets the text shown above the NPC. Put names containing spaces in quotes:

/hcnpc set merchant lumberjack "Peter der Holzhändler"

Omit the display name to keep the current one. Names allow 1–128 characters without control characters. On the first change, Core records the original name permanently.

With three arguments, a registered job in the first position means job typ name. Otherwise the arguments mean identifier job typ. Use the entity UUID when a saved key matches a registered job.

docs.title: Reset an NPC
docs.text:
Aim at the NPC or specify an identifier:

/hcnpc reset
/hcnpc reset <identifier>

Reset removes all HcNpcs actions and restores the recorded name. If the NPC had no nameplate, reset removes the added name. If there was no previous rename, the native name stays as is. The NPC remains in the world.

A saved key can be reset while the NPC is unloaded. The original name is restored when it loads. Core keeps a disabled entry to prevent old assignments from returning after restart. A new set reactivates it.

docs.title: Other commands
docs.text: /hcnpc lists assignments and /hcnpc reload reloads them from Core. The only administrative subcommands are set, reset, and reload. Use native Hytale tools for spawning, models, positioning, and physical behavior.

docs.title: Interaction prompt
docs.text:
HcNpcs advertises Hytale's native prompt for enabled NPCs with an available action. Merchants show the trade hint. Hytale displays the client's configured Use key, usually F, when the player aims at the NPC within range.

After reset or when the provider is unavailable, HcNpcs clears the added hints within about one second. The hints use native replication and require neither a custom HUD nor a persistent Interactable flag.

Command results appear as Core notifications. The configured messages are NPC Gespeichert on success and NPC Aktion Fehlgeschlagen on failure. Help and the binding list appear in chat.

The command help and arguments in the game are in English, for example type, identifier-or-job and type-or-name. The result notifications remain German.

docs.title: Configure interaction distance
docs.text:
HcNpcs creates HcNpcs/config.json in the plugin data directory:

{
  "interactionDistanceMeters": 3.0
}

The setting applies to all HcNpcs bindings. It limits opening, subsequent UI actions, crosshair selection, and HcNpcs-added hints. The accepted range is 0.5 to 10 meters. Run /hcnpc reload after editing. Invalid values leave the last valid setting and file intact.

Administrative changes using a saved identifier still work from farther away. Native hints and client-side targeting have their own limits. Increasing this setting does not extend native targeting.

docs.title: PlayerHudPlugin
docs.text:
The centered HUD in the upper-right corner shows the player name, money, overall player level, and active profession with its level, XP within the level, and progress bar. It hides the profession section when none is active.

The world clock displays the current world's in-game time in 24-hour HH:mm format. It follows the player across world changes.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
PlayerHud enables the display once per connection after PlayerReadyEvent. /hud toggles it for the current connection. Further ready events preserve that choice. The HUD is visible again on the next join.

The wooden background is stored in Hud/PlayerHudPanel.png. The HUD shows /inbox and the unread count for the inbox.

docs.title: Data and UI
docs.text:
HudService reads balance, player level, and active profession about once per second through PlayerService, PlayerLevelService, and ProfessionService.activeProfession. Queries run on the HUD worker. GeneralPlayerHud sends UI updates when snapshots change. The UI is in Hud/PlayerHud.ui. HUD and session references are cleared on disconnect.

See the UI and HUD contracts.

docs.title: PlayerStatsPlugin
docs.text: PlayerStats collects player events and persists batches through Core. PlayerStats counts joins and leaves. Core creates player profiles.

docs.title: Tracked values
docs.text:
• Blocks placed and broken.
  • Interactions and items picked up through interactions.
  • Joins, leaves, and their first event timestamps.
  • Actual health lost or damage dealt after applying damage rules.
  • Deaths and items lost on death.
  • Distance traveled, accounting for world and session boundaries and unusual position jumps.

Per-opponent kill counts and a full PvP kill history would require a separate extension to the current delta and entity contract.

docs.title: Persistence
docs.text:
Events write to an in-memory buffer. A single writer flushes roughly every five seconds, retaining the same batch ID on retries. Core applies each batch atomically and idempotently. Disconnect and shutdown also trigger writes.

A hard crash before a confirmed flush can lose buffered events. Batch receipts prevent duplicate application in the database.

docs.title: ProtectionPlugin
docs.text: ProtectionPlugin associates registered areas with allowed and blocked actions. Shared area data and decisions live in Core.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
• /protection register <areaName> <actionType> registers an area for an action type.
  • /protection remove <areaName> removes a registration. Hytale command help shows the optional action type.
  • /protection list lists registrations.

Use the action types accepted by the server implementation.

docs.title: Integration
docs.text:
Area protection and plot ownership are separate rules. For new gameplay actions, decide which checks apply in each world. Recheck protection on the server when a player clicks a UI button.

Minigames will need additional session and world rules. A shared game-mode context is still planned. Verify administrative access against the registered Hytale commands.

docs.title: TeleportPlugin
docs.text: TeleportPlugin manages teleport requests between players.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
• /tpa <player> requests a teleport.
  • /tpaccept accepts the matching request.
  • /tpdeny rejects it.

Requests are temporary. Before teleporting, verify the current player session and destination world.

docs.title: Display
docs.text:
The current TpaService uses EventTitleUtil to display a title with instructions for accepting and declining. The Teleport repository currently has no dedicated .ui file. Titles are separate from custom pages and PlayerHud.

Future minigames will need to validate the shared session context before sending or accepting requests. A central game-mode restriction is still planned. See the minigame design.

docs.title: WarpPlugin
docs.text: WarpPlugin provides fixed destinations via /warp city, /warp farmworld, and /warp spawn.

docs.title: Integration
docs.text:
These commands use the corresponding worlds in the Hytale Universe. Each world must exist and be prepared. FarmWorldPlugin owns the farm world's lifecycle. Warp handles the teleport itself.

The current manifest declares no Core dependency. Future minigame rules need to prevent players from leaving an active round or carrying its inventory out through a general warp command.

Check destinations and positions before changing a server setup. A teleport can fail if the destination world is missing or being recreated.

docs.title: Custom assets
docs.text:
The shared HytaleCity:Assets pack is in hytale-city-assets. Install HytaleCity.Assets in the server's asset pack or mods directory. When installing from a ZIP, place the manifest at the root of the archive. On update, replace the previous pack and restart the server.

Item IDs are the filenames under Server/Item/Items without the .json extension. Use them with /give, quest deliveries, and reward lists. Block sets, hitboxes, and particles have their own asset types. Models, textures, icons, and UI documents are referenced by resource path.

Core supports the migration to HC_ IDs for known database references. Check existing items and blocks in world data separately. Mappings for former IDs and resource paths are in the pack's development directory.

docs.title: Ownership and thread contract
docs.text:
Core owns the XP curve, authoritative progression, repositories, transactions, operation receipts, reward definitions, earned claims and payouts. LevelPlugin is a Hytale adapter: config, legacy-file import, world-thread events, and the existing inventory helper. The public XP mutators in its LevelService now return CompletableFuture<ExpChangeResult>. No other shared plugin currently calls those mutators. Do not block a world thread with join() or get().

Use MainCore.getBean(AsyncLevelService.class) from other Hytale plugins. Core's bounded worker pool completes a future only after transaction commit. Queue-full, stopped worker, invalid requests and database errors complete exceptionally. Never announce success before the future completes. Continuations run on worker threads; schedule inventory, world and UI actions on the owning Hytale world executor.

var levels = MainCore.getBean(AsyncLevelService.class);
UUID operationId = existingGameplayEventId; // retain this ID for retries
levels.load(playerUuid).thenCompose(ignored ->
    levels.grantRawExp(playerUuid, operationId, 150L)
).whenComplete((change, error) -> {
    // error: report failure; success: database commit has already completed.
});

LevelProgressionService is the blocking transactional API for background workers:

  • getProgress, getLevel, getExpInLevel, getOverflowExp, getRemainingXp, getProgress01, isMaxLevel read authoritative state.
  • getCachedProgress never queries the database. It returns an optional immutable snapshot and is suitable for HUD polling. Local cache publication happens only after commit, including mutations made directly by other plugins through Core.
  • requiredXp, totalXpToLevel, getPolicy expose curve information.
  • grantRawExp, grantScaledExp, grantPercent, removeExp, setLevel, setExpInLevel perform atomic changes under a database row lock.
  • apply accepts a stable operation UUID for every action, including setters. Same ID + same request returns the stored result with replayed=true; a different request using that ID fails. Retries do not repeat XP or reward issuance.
  • AsyncLevelService offers async counterparts and generic apply plus loading, refresh, pending rewards, claiming and reward synchronization.
  • PlayerLevelService initializes/imports raw persisted state. Its snapshot save method is low-level persistence, not the gameplay API: it bypasses XP rules, operation receipts, reward issuance and progression-cache publication.

Initialize new players using AsyncLevelService.load. Direct Core mutations require an existing level row. Initialization failures never fabricate a level-one cache. The local read cache is not a cross-server notification bus; use refresh after remote-server mutations if running the same UUID on multiple servers. Concurrent committed mutations are protected by database row locks, even across servers. Chain dependent operations with thenCompose; independent concurrent calls do not promise submission order. Administrative callers must enforce their own permissions.

docs.title: Curve and XP semantics
docs.text:
Default max level is 50. The curve retains the original coefficients and stitches quadratic sections together at levels 10 and 30, eliminating the previous resets. Default XP requirements are 150 (level 1), 951 (10), 1085 (11), 8951 (30), 9299 (31) and 26551 (50). Actual pacing still depends on XP sources and session lengths. LevelPolicy validates finite scaling and overflow settings, strictly increasing coefficients, arithmetic limits, and level range. LevelPlugin configures this Core policy at setup using only maxLevel, startLevel and scalingExponent from config.json. Curve coefficients and the overflow-cap multiplier are fixed Core defaults. Valid legacy configs are rewritten to those three supported fields at startup; obsolete autosave/debug/curve/overflow settings are removed. Malformed or invalid files remain unchanged while the plugin falls back to defaults.

scalingExponent affects XP awarded by scaled grants, not the level thresholds. The scaled amount is rounded from baseXp * (requiredXp(currentLevel) / requiredXp(1))^scalingExponent. With exponent 0, no level-based award scaling is applied; 0.35 gives moderate scaling, not a fixed 35% increase per level. For example, 100 base XP at level 10 becomes approximately 191 XP. Raw XP grants remain unscaled. The fixed quadratic curve independently determines XP required for each next level (150, 191 and 244 XP at levels 1, 2 and 3).

Reaching a threshold exactly levels up immediately, carries remaining XP forward, and may cross multiple levels in one operation. Reaching level 50 exactly does not invent overflow XP. Additional XP at max level goes to overflow using the existing award-based diminishing-return rule; at max the displayed progress is 100%. XP removals consume overflow first and clamp at level 1; effectiveDelta reports only XP actually removed. Negative/non-finite values and arithmetic overflow fail the entire transaction. grantPercent accepts [0,1] of the current level's cap. setExpInLevel resets current-level XP and applies the specified amount, including normal threshold crossings; at max level use grant/remove for overflow instead. A lower configured max than an existing player's level rejects mutations rather than silently deleting progress. No existing player is reset by changing the curve.

docs.title: Crash semantics
docs.text:
There is no write-behind/autosave window. A successful future means that XP, new reward entitlements and the idempotency receipt committed together. Losing the server process or its in-memory cache after that point does not require a shutdown save to recover progression. A crash before commit/future acknowledgement may have an unknown outcome: retry with the same operation ID. Pending queued work is not a durable queue and is not described as successfully applied. This assumes durable MariaDB/InnoDB commit settings; database-host loss and storage failure still require normal database durability/backups.

player_xp_operations retains receipts to make retries safe. It grows with the number of requests. Do not delete receipts blindly: removing one also removes its idempotency guarantee. Configure a deliberate archival/retention policy once event rates and the maximum retry horizon are known.

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
No economy amounts are silently seeded. Define rewards through Core at setup or from an admin tool:

var rewards = MainCore.getBean(LevelRewardService.class);
rewards.defineReward("level.5.money", 5, 500L, null);
rewards.defineReward("level.10.title", 10, 0L, "title:explorer");

defineReward and setEnabled manage definitions. Every intermediate level crossed by a successful progression transaction records earned rewards. Each player/key pair is unique. Losing and regaining a level cannot earn the same reward twice. Already earned rewards snapshot the original amount/entitlement; changing or disabling a definition does not rewrite or revoke an existing claim.

listRewards, listPendingRewards, claim, and synchronizeAvailableRewards expose reward state. Async loading synchronizes rewards for imported players, starting levels and newly added definitions. Explicit synchronization is available for online players after definition changes. Earned/pending rewards survive logout, cache eviction and process restart. Claiming does not require retaining the level once it was legitimately earned.

A claim's money payout and claimedAt marker commit in one transaction. Concurrent claims or retries return newlyClaimed=false after the first payout. Missing player accounts, balance overflow or transaction failures leave the reward pending. An entitlement is a durable unlock record that other plugins can read; it is not an arbitrary callback that can deliver an item twice after a crash.

Physical inventory items and arbitrary external commands are deliberately not run inside reward transactions. Exactly-once item delivery requires a separate Hytale inventory reconciliation/idempotency design; marking a DB claim then giving an item (or vice versa) cannot provide that guarantee. LevelService.giveItem remains a raw inventory helper, not a durable level-reward claim API.

docs.title: Events, deployment and validation
docs.text:
LevelPlugin emits its gameplay callbacks on the owning world executor after commit. It emits one LevelUp/LevelDown event per intermediate level. Listener failures are isolated and cannot undo committed XP or suppress durable reward claims. These callbacks are cosmetic/gameplay notifications, not durable delivery records. Direct Core calls update the Core read cache and rewards but do not emit LevelPlugin's local callbacks; callers should rely on the returned change or reward records.

Deploy new CorePlugin and LevelPlugin together. Core creates tables through versioned Liquibase migrations, then Hibernate validates the schema. Legacy JSON files are imported idempotently at setup and remain unchanged backups, never a live backend. HUD job levels use the independent Core JobService; no existing global-level caller was found in other shared plugin sources. Its current global label is literal Jobs. Tests use H2 transactions and concurrent workers; live MariaDB/Hytale acceptance must verify plugin startup, schema creation/import, XP grants and reward claims.

docs.title: HcNpcs
docs.text: Hytale 0.7.7 NPC runtime. Install CorePlugin, HcNpcs and JobsPlugin together when updating this feature. Jobs now declares a required HcNpcs dependency; the reflective listener and duplicate Jobs packet hook have been removed.

docs.title: Ownership and persistence
docs.text:
• Core owns hc_npcs, hc_npc_actions and migration from jobs_npc_job_keys.
  • Hytale owns every NPC's spawning, movement and world persistence. HcNpcs only attaches actions and optional names to existing native entity UUIDs.
  • Runtime bindings require role == null and an entity UUID. Historical managed definitions with a role, including invalid test roles such as holzfaeller, stay in the DB for inspection but are ignored on startup and every refresh. No automatic spawn, despawn, role validation, chunk loading or spawn retry exists in HcNpcs.
  • Native bindings, including disabled reset tombstones, remain cached so deferred original-name restoration works when the NPC loads.
  • Import is idempotent and leaves the old table intact. Existing definitions, including intentionally reset mappings, win over legacy mappings.
  • Name changes run on world queues. All database work goes through Core on the HcNpcs IO worker.

docs.title: Admin commands
docs.text:
Spawn NPCs with native Hytale tools first. Permission: hcnpcs.admin.

/hcnpc
/hcnpc set merchant lumberjack
/hcnpc set merchant lumberjack "Holz Haendler"
/hcnpc set <ENTITY_UUID_OR_SAVED_KEY> merchant miner
/hcnpc set <ENTITY_UUID_OR_SAVED_KEY> merchant miner "Erz Haendler"
/hcnpc reset
/hcnpc reset <ENTITY_UUID_OR_SAVED_KEY>
/hcnpc reload

Without an identifier, set/reset uses the NPC under the crosshair within the configured interaction distance (three metres by default). Explicit identifiers take precedence. New UUID bindings require a loaded real NPC in the same world. Existing keys may be assigned without a name, or reset, while unloaded. A new name requires the NPC to be loaded so its original Nameplate can be captured safely. Names with spaces must be quoted; names must contain 1-128 characters and no control characters. With three set arguments, a registered job in first position means job type name; otherwise they mean identifier job type. Saved keys matching registered job names should use the unambiguous entity UUID instead.

Names are stored atomically with the action in Core and applied through Hytale's Nameplate component, making them visible above the NPC. Omitting the name preserves it. The first overridden native name (including an absent nameplate) is recorded durably. Reset clears all plugin actions, disables dispatch and restores that original name on the world queue, also after restart/unload. The native NPC remains in the world. A disabled tombstone prevents old mappings from being reimported; set reactivates it. Historical managed definitions are ignored and cannot be selected through HcNpcs.

Only set, reset and reload remain as admin subcommands. create, action, configure, removeaction and move are removed. Native tools/role assets own models, position and physical behaviour. HcNpcs no longer applies Frozen/invulnerability/model changes to attached native NPCs. The former create/move/configure runtime APIs are removed as well. Old physical overrides already present on an attached NPC are not automatically reconstructed or undone; use native tools if needed.

The older Jobs one-shot selection API and /job admin npcset remain compatible; it is not needed for the new immediate crosshair commands.

docs.title: Plugin API
docs.text:
HcNpcsService npcs = HcNpcsAPI.getService();
Registration registration = npcs.registerAction(
    "MyQuestPlugin", "quests:giver", "Quests",
    (player, definition, entityUuid, questGroup) -> {
        // Called on the player's world thread after NPC/world/range validation.
        // Open the custom quest UI here. Load DB data asynchronously first.
    }
);
// In plugin shutdown:
registration.close(); // idempotent; alternatively unregisterOwner("MyQuestPlugin")

assign and reset return futures for atomic named assignments and reset. setAction, attachAction, removeAction and reload also return futures. HcNpcs exposes no create/move/configure API. Never join these futures on a world thread. Future completions run on an IO thread: queue ECS/UI operations with world.execute, then recheck player session, NPC binding and range using validate(world, player, entityUuid). definitions() and findByEntity() return immutable cached snapshots. entityUuid(key) resolves the current binding; always validate it before ECS use.

Duplicate action registrations are rejected. Registration handles remove only their own instance, so closing an old handle cannot unregister a replacement. A single action opens directly; several available actions show a custom selection page. Missing providers do not run. The chooser rechecks target and current binding on submit and expires after two minutes. A quest provider is an extension point, not an implemented quest system.

docs.title: Interaction and UI
docs.text:
One retained inbound watcher recognizes Use interaction targets, limits scheduling to once per player per 250 ms, and is deregistered on shutdown. All target resolution happens on the captured world queue. It verifies the current PlayerRef/store/world, an actual NPC component and the configured interaction distance (three metres by default). Only persisted bindings dispatch actions. Internal exceptions are logged with their cause; implementation details are not sent to players.

Jobs loads the profession and merchant snapshots on its IO worker. ProfessionUI validates NPC proximity and the current session before handling actions. The merchant provides selling, limited stock purchases, profession activation, quests and milestone claims.

At the merchant, choose an inventory item and quantity and confirm the displayed total. The command /job sell uses the same coordinator with a two-step confirmation for the held item. The previous shop and upgrade screen is accessible via /job <jobKey>.

docs.title: Sale consistency and recovery
docs.text:
Core's JobSaleService credits money for current sales in one transaction, serialized per player and deduplicated by operation UUID. Normal balance setters/deposits/withdrawals use the same player row lock; transfers lock both players in UUID order and reject overflow. Unrelated Player updates use dynamic SQL updates so they do not write stale balances. Jobs uses additive adjustXp and an explicit unlock operation for existing entry/upgrade/reward paths; player_jobs.version provides an additional optimistic guard for legacy detached job writes. Liquibase owns the schema; Hibernate validates it after migration. player_jobs.version has default zero. The Jobs coordinator reserves exact planned slots/stacks on the world thread, preserving metadata/durability in compensation. prepare returns true only for a newly created operation; an existing operation returns false and must never trigger another inventory removal. Preparation stores a BSON inventory plan before removal. Changed slots cancel the sale before removal. Arithmetic overflow rolls back all DB effects.

Inventory/world saving and MariaDB cannot share a transaction. A crash between reservation and commit therefore requires reconciliation rather than an automatic payout/refund:

  • PREPARED: removal may or may not have happened. Check the recorded inventoryEvidence, actual inventory and logs before taking action.
  • COMMITTED: DB rewards were applied. Never automatically refund this operation.
  • REFUND_DUE: compensation is outstanding or may have been partially returned. Inspect actual inventory; do not blindly restore the whole plan.
  • ABORTED: no payout remains and the caller confirmed compensation/no removal.

abort grants a physical refund only on its first PREPARED-to-REFUND_DUE transition; repeated calls never authorize returning the same items again. Core provides pending(playerUuid), diagnostic(operationUuid), idempotent commit(request), abort(request) and confirmRefund(request) for explicit reconciliation. confirmRefund must only be called after actual item restitution (or verified absence of removal). Unresolved operations block further sales for that player. Ambiguous outcomes log the operation UUID and remain recorded. Receipt retention/archival must preserve deduplication and all unresolved records.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Core tests cover migration, immutable snapshots, optimistic bindings, movement ownership, action limits, atomic rewards, rollback, concurrent replay, stale job writes, opposing transfers, concurrent deposits/XP changes and unresolved sales. HcNpcs tests cover action registration/cleanup, command inputs and ignored legacy spawn definitions on repeated reloads. Jobs tests cover exact inventory plans, changed items and compensation failures.

Maven cannot validate Hytale's client UI DSL or a live world. Before production acceptance, test native spawn/set/name/reset/restart/chunk unload, both merchant confirmation paths, movement during UI loads and plugin shutdown on a Hytale 0.7.7 test server. The UI files reuse native Common.ui templates and send only server-defined action values.

docs.title: Short NPC duty commands
docs.text:
/hcnpc set [identifier] <job> <typ> uses plain command arguments, for example merchant lumberjack or merchant miner. The duty is resolved against registered providers; the command does not hardcode a merchant-only switch. Only merchant is currently registered by Jobs. A future provider can register job:worker and use the same command after adding its implementation.

Stored keys use singular job:merchant and canonical type arguments such as typ:lumberjack. Current type names are farmer, lumberjack, hunter, miner, cook, and fisher; Core maps these to the existing profession keys without renaming job progress. Old jobs:merchant bindings with German profession arguments migrate idempotently on startup. Generic namespaced actions such as quests:giver forest remain supported. Unregistered duties and unknown profession types are rejected before saving.

docs.title: Selection and verification
docs.text: /hcnpc lists saved keys and entity UUIDs. Display names, role IDs and model IDs are not unique entity identifiers. New bindings currently use legacy.<UUID> keys for persistence compatibility. Set/reset use Hytale native positional command variants; tests cover registration, ambiguity, name validation, original-name preservation, rollback and reset tombstones. Live crosshair/nameplate/UI/restart checks are still required.

docs.title: Native interaction prompt
docs.text:
Enabled native NPC bindings with an available action advertise Hytale's native interactable hint to their current entity viewers. Merchants use server.interactionHints.trade; other providers use server.interactionHints.generic. The client draws the crosshair/key prompt with its configured Use binding (normally F). Existing native Interactable components and their hints are preserved.

Hints use the native EntityViewer/InteractableUpdate replication path, without persisting an Interactable component or adding a custom HUD. The world queue refreshes visible-viewer hints once per second, including newly connected viewers. Reset, removed/unavailable actions and shutdown remove only HcNpcs-added client hints; native interactability is retained. Live client visibility, key remapping and interaction tests are still required.

Command results use Core NotificationUtility: success displays NPC Gespeichert, failure displays NPC Aktion Fehlgeschlagen. Help and the binding list remain chat output.

Command descriptions, argument hints and usage placeholders are in English (type, identifier-or-job, job-or-type, type-or-name). Result notifications retain the configured German wording.

docs.title: Interaction distance configuration
docs.text:
HcNpcs creates HcNpcs/config.json in its short plugin data directory:

{
  "interactionDistanceMeters": 3.0
}

Edit the value and run /hcnpc reload to apply it without restarting. Accepted range: 0.5 to 10 metres. Invalid reloads retain the last valid value and leave the file unchanged; startup logs invalid settings and uses the default. The same distance gates crosshair selection, Use/action dispatch, UI validation and HcNpcs-added viewer hints. Explicit administrative identifiers can still update/reset stored bindings without standing beside the NPC. Hytale's own pre-existing hints/client targeting may impose their own presentation limits; setting a larger server limit does not extend native client targeting automatically.
